archetype.name: Pocket Passer (veteran backup)
archetype.definition: A big, 11-year statuesque-by-now passer who wins from the pocket between the numbers and in the intermediate game, now the Vikings' QB2 behind Kyler Murray, asked to steer a run-leaning offense that leans on the league's best defense.

report.headline: Efficient numbers on a tiny sample, built on a few big throws and sacks
report.take:
Carson Wentz is the Vikings' insurance policy, not their plan. Kyler Murray has started every game but Week 2. Wentz's season is the relief appearance in the Week 1 win over Green Bay, where he played 83% of snaps, plus a 9-3 grinder in Chicago. That is 48 dropbacks. On paper the efficiency looks strong: 8.24 adjusted net yards per dropback (12th of 45), 0.122 EPA per dropback (16th), no interceptions, and a 7.7% TD rate that ranks 4th. Read that as two games, not a season.

The efficiency comes from a handful of plays. His three deep attempts added 5.1 EPA. His two no-huddle snaps added 6.9, more than his whole dropback total of 4.6. Justin Jefferson's 14 targets produced 13 EPA, and the middle of the field (0.894 EPA per attempt) carried nearly everything. Take away the big throws and what's left is ordinary or worse. His -7.79 CPOE ranks 41st of 45, a 20.5% bad-throw rate ranks 37th of 38, and on throws under 10 air yards he's 13.3 points under expected. His one start, the Chicago game, is the cleaner read: 0.022 EPA per dropback, roughly league average (0.04), with no touchdowns.

The sacks are the real story. A 13.3% sack rate is last among 45 qualifiers, and two-thirds of his pressures became sacks. That isn't new. His pressure-to-sack rate was 37.1% in 2022 and 39.6% last year, both near the bottom of the league. He doesn't scramble his way out of it either: 4.2% of dropbacks, -0.437 EPA per scramble, and no first downs on them. He holds the ball and takes the hit. The legs that made him a dual-threat in Philadelphia are mostly gone (0.63 yards per carry this year).

The conclusion: if Murray misses time, Minnesota gets a passer who can hit Jefferson and T.J. Hockenson over the middle and won't give the ball away. But he will stall drives with sacks, and his accuracy has slipped from last year's +1.1 CPOE. Behind a top-ranked defense, that's enough to win low-scoring games, as the Chicago start showed. Don't expect the Week 1 three-touchdown line to repeat.

strengths.title: Intermediate and middle-of-field throws
strengths.body: When he pushes the ball 10+ yards, and especially over the middle, he's been productive: 0.673 EPA per attempt on throws of 10+ air yards, with CPOE right at expected there. That fits his career; his best seasons came from driving the ball into the intermediate zone. On 15 attempts, it's a pattern consistent with who he's been rather than proof.

strengths.title: Feeding Jefferson and Hockenson
strengths.body: His two main targets have turned their looks into big value: Jefferson at 0.931 EPA per target and Hockenson at 0.902. That's mostly talent around him, not something he creates. It's also why a Wentz start isn't a disaster for the passing game: the ball goes where it should.

strengths.title: No turnovers so far
strengths.body: Zero interceptions on 39 attempts ranks 1st, and his aggressiveness (12.8%) is down from last season. That is a cleaner profile than 2025's five picks in five games. Expect some interceptions to return with volume, but this conservative version fits an offense built around its defense.

concerns.title: Sacks are a long-running trait
concerns.body: He's last of 45 in sack rate, and 66.7% of his pressures became sacks. That is extreme on a small sample, but the direction matches his recent seasons near the bottom of the league in pressure-to-sack. These sacks don't come from extending plays for big scrambles; his scrambles have lost value. He's likely to keep taking more sacks than average, though not this many.

concerns.title: Short-area accuracy has slipped
concerns.body: His CPOE is down 8.9 points from last season. On short throws he's 12.2 points below expected, and his bad-throw rate is near the bottom. Some of that is noise on 24 short attempts. Still, missing the easy completions is what turns an offense ranked 32nd in success rate into three-and-outs.

concerns.title: Efficiency rests on a few plays
concerns.body: Two no-huddle snaps and three deep balls account for more EPA than his whole set of dropbacks. In his one full start, his EPA per dropback was near league average. The headline efficiency ranks are fragile.

trend.note: A sharp Week 1 in relief (5.0 passing EPA, three touchdowns) gave way to a 0.5-EPA grind in his Week 2 start at Chicago. He hasn't taken a snap in the log since Murray returned in Week 3.

nextGame.headline: Backup unless Murray sits, but Detroit's pass defense is soft
nextGame.body:
Wentz is listed as QB2, and Murray started Week 7 with no injury designation in the dossier, so the baseline is that he doesn't play. If he does, the matchup suits his strengths. Detroit ranks 28th in pass-defense EPA and 28th against deep throws, allows the most fantasy points to quarterbacks, and has been gashed by tight ends and second receivers. The catch is the pass rush: Detroit's sack rate ranks 7th, and that hits his worst trait directly. The game is indoors, Minnesota is a 3-point underdog, and Detroit's offense ranks 3rd, so a trailing script could push the passing volume up.

On Minnesota's side, guard Donovan Jackson (77% of snaps) is on injured reserve, which weakens the interior protection in front of a sack-prone passer. Aaron Jones is questionable but described as day-to-day. If Jones sits, the run game ranked 27th in EPA leans even more on the pass. For Detroit, safety Kerby Joseph is out and corner Ennis Rakestraw is questionable, which thins a secondary already allowing explosive passes at a high rate.

keyMatchups.title: Middle-field throws vs. Detroit's secondary
keyMatchups.body: His production lives over the middle and at 10+ yards. Detroit ranks 28th in deep EPA allowed and 31st in fantasy points over average to TE1s. Hockenson up the seam is the cleanest path.

keyMatchups.title: Detroit's rush vs. his sack habit
keyMatchups.body: Detroit's defense is poor overall but gets home, with a sack rate ranking 7th. Against a quarterback who turns pressure into sacks this often, that's the swing factor for drive success.

nextGame.watch: Kyler Murray's status this week. Without a Murray absence, Wentz stays on the sideline.

restOfSeason.body:
The most likely outcome is a handful of snaps or none. His value is as a fill-in, and the dossier gives no reason to expect Murray to miss time. If Wentz does start, expect something like his Chicago game rather than his Week 1 relief. In those starts, project roughly 170-235 passing yards and about one touchdown a game, with two to four sacks. The offense is run-leaning (24th in pass rate over expected) and leans on a defense ranked 1st in EPA, so volume will be modest unless the game script forces it.

The touchdown rate (4th) and zero interceptions will regress with more attempts, and CPOE should drift back toward his career norm of roughly even, which would help. The sack problem is the part to trust; it has been building for several seasons.
swingFactors: Interior line protection with Jackson on IR
Whether CPOE recovers toward his career norm

confidence.note: 48 dropbacks across two games, one start, and a backup role.
